claims.text: Traditional single-phase ZrB2 requires processing temperatures at or above approximately 2300 °C.
ZrB2 sintered at approximately 1700 °C has microstructural or defect-related vulnerabilities relative to ZrB2 sintered at or above 2300 °C.
Lower-temperature ZrB2 has a more reactive surface that is prone to oxidation.
Lower-temperature manufactured ZrB2 is vulnerable to liquid plating-metal corrosion.
SPS at approximately 1700 °C under an inert atmosphere can produce dense, single-phase ZrB2.
ALD at temperatures below 300 °C can provide a thin, conformal, high-quality 100–300 nm Al2O3 coating on densified ZrB2.
The ALD treatment will form a continuous, dense Al2O3 surface layer that acts as a diffusion barrier.
Al2O3 has high-temperature stability.
Al2O3 has low oxygen diffusivity.
Al2O3 is chemically inert toward liquid plating metals such as Pb-based baths.
The Al2O3 coating will prevent or slow oxygen ingress into lower-temperature-sintered ZrB2.
The Al2O3 coating will prevent or slow attack of ZrB2 by corrosive liquid plating metals.
Blocking oxygen and plating-metal attack will preserve the underlying ZrB2 microstructure and mechanical properties.
A nanoscale Al2O3 coating can compensate for lower densification and surface flaws caused by lower-temperature manufacture.
Coated lower-temperature ZrB2 will exhibit significantly lower oxidation weight gain than uncoated lower-temperature ZrB2.
Coated lower-temperature ZrB2 will form fewer deleterious surface oxides than uncoated lower-temperature ZrB2.
Coated lower-temperature ZrB2 will undergo minimal degradation in a liquid plating-metal bath.
The hardness and structural integrity of coated lower-temperature ZrB2 will be comparable to or better than those of traditionally high-temperature-sintered ZrB2.
The coated components can operate continuously at approximately 1500 °C in oxidizing atmospheres.
The coated components can operate for prolonged periods in contact with a liquid plating-metal bath.

contradictions.description: The substrate is described as dense or fully densified, while the proposed coating is also said to compensate for lower densification. It is unclear whether residual porosity or deficient densification is actually present.
